question.text: An <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>-particle (mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> amu) and a singly charged Sulphur ion (mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>32</mn></math> amu) are initially at rest. They are accelerated through a potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi></math> and then allowed to pass into a region of uniform magnetic field which is normal to the velocities of the particles. Within this region, the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math>-particle and the sulphur ion move in circular orbits of radii <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>S</mi></msub></math>, respectively. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></mfrac></mfenced></math> is __________ .

solution.text:
When a particle moves on a circular path in a magnetic field then,

∵R=mvqB=2mEqB=2mqVqB=2mVqB

According to given data,

∵V=constant& B=constant

∴R∝mq

RαRS=mαqα×qSmS=42×132

⇒RαRS=116=14

Then, RSRα=4
